verdict.rationale: LangSmith documents a Playground service that forwards requests to various LLM APIs, including custom model servers, and lists prompt engineering as a core platform capability. So prompts can be run against real models, but the evidence only describes this in a self-hosting architecture context. Missing for 10: documentation of prompt variables/templating in the playground, details of the iterative editing and comparison workflow, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can iterate on prompts in a playground against real models and variables

citations.quote: The Playground is a service that handles forwarding requests to various LLM APIs... This can also be used to connect to your own custom model servers.
Host an instance of LangSmith in your own infrastructure for observability, evaluation, and prompt engineering.
